narrative.body: 6 metrics are tracked over the period; each panel states where it started and where it ended. The shared y-scale spans (1 621) to 1 908, a span of 3 529, in R'000; a panel's percentage of it is its own axis, both ends printed, over that span.

notes.heading: Scale
notes.body: Net profit and Cash share one y-scale, so neither of them can look like it moved more than it did. Revenue (1.0%) and Operating expenses (1.6%) (too little of it to register) and Gross margin and Debtor days (different units) are on their OWN scales, so their slopes are not comparable with the shared-scale panels.

notes.heading: Period
notes.body: Each panel plots one MONTH. The same measures print for the WHOLE reporting period, against the comparative — revenue, gross margin and operating expenses on the income statement page, net profit on the group results page, cash on the cash page and debtor days on the scorecard page. Different windows: the two will not agree. Debtor days also differs in its annualisation, which the basis of preparation defines. A ratio ending in the part month is taken on the days posted, so its level is not comparable with the months before it.

Trade payables over cost of sales, times 365 — annualised, whatever the length of the reporting period. Not reported where there is no cost of sales.
Debtor days plus inventory days, less creditor days — each annualised on 365 days, as above. Not reported where no account is classified as inventory.
Cash generated by operations before investing and financing activities.
Scored against the platform's default target. A metric with no target is unscored rather than assumed met; one the figures cannot support is not meaningful. Neither counts as a pass or a miss.
